cause.label: litigation_or_regulatory
cause.what_happened: Rosen Law Firm filed a securities class action (Chance v. Netcapital, D. Mass. 1:26-cv-14584) on 2026-10-08 that repeats the SEC's August revenue-fraud allegations. On 2026-10-09 a wave of law-firm press releases (Rosen, Gainey McKenna and others) went out, and the stock gapped -17.9% at the open before recovering +7.9% intraday on 0.75x normal volume. This came after a catalyst-less +45.9% on 10-07 and -17.6% on 10-08 in a low-float momentum name, so part of the move is the whipsaw itself.

findings.finding: Law-firm press releases advertising the 2026-10-08 securities class action began on 10-08/10-09 and, on the usual Rosen-style cadence before a 2026-12-07 lead-plaintiff deadline, will keep running through Monday 2026-10-12.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Firms issue these releases daily after a first filing. Monday's batch will land on retail screens inside the window. The suit merely restates the SEC complaint of 2026-08-10, so the information is old and only the headline flow is new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 10-08, the day of the Rosen filing, the stock closed -17.6% (following a +45.9% day); on 10-09 it gapped -17.9% and then recovered +7.9% intraday. The SEC complaint disclosure in August: 08-11 -12.9%, 08-18 -28.5% (baseline events).
findings.why_not_priced: The first day of releases is in today's price, but later days are not, and a low-float retail name reacts to headline counts rather than to new facts. If the flow were fully priced, today's +7.9% intraday recovery would not have happened while the releases were still going out.

findings.finding: NCPL has closed at or above $1.00 on 12 consecutive sessions (2026-09-23 to 2026-10-08), past the 10-business-day cure in Nasdaq's 2026-08-07 bid-price letter, so a compliance-regained notice and its press release can land at any time, including 2026-10-12.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The 10th qualifying close was 2026-10-06. Nasdaq normally confirms a cure within days, and the company has press-released every Nasdaq letter (08-10, 08-28, 09-25). Nasdaq may extend the test to 20 business days at its discretion, which the 8-K itself states, so the timing is not certain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The company has no prior bid-price cure on record. Its Nasdaq deficiency releases were followed by +31% (2026-08-28, per ts2.tech) and -20.6% (09-28, after the 09-25 release), so this line produces no consistent sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Traders can count closes, but a formal notice removes one of three listing clocks and would make a retail headline. A priced cure would show as no reaction to the release. The size is kept small because the timing cannot be dated and the separate delinquent-filing clock (plan due 10-23) stays open.

findings.finding: No registered offering or ATM can price overnight. The company is delinquent on its FY2026 10-K and 10-Q (Nasdaq letter 2026-09-21), its FY2022-2025 audited statements are subject to non-reliance (8-K 2026-08-18), and its only effective S-1 is a resale of warrants struck at $2.03-$8.75, far above the $1.16 spot.
findings.mechanism_in_window: This holds through the whole window: the company cannot produce a usable prospectus before 2026-10-12 without audited financials. Private convertible notes (Item 3.02) remain possible and are not ruled out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 financings were all private convertible notes (8-Ks of 05-01, 05-18, 06-10 x2, 06-16, 07-08), not registered takedowns. EDGAR full-text search finds no 'at-the-market' language after the S-1/A of 2026-03-24.
findings.why_not_priced: The base rate for fallers includes names that get an overnight offering as a second shoe. This name structurally cannot, which separates it from the cross-section the ranking is measured against. The offsetting risk is a private note, which is why the finding is small.
